cita: Kong et al. (2025). MapAgent: Trajectory-Constructed Memory-Augmented Planning for Mobile Task Automation.
problema: LLM-based mobile GUI agents lack real-world knowledge of specific apps, causing hallucinations and ineffective planning because they cannot remember prior interactions with an app and must re-explore it from scratch each time.
mecanismo: A trajectory-based memory mechanism (WRITE) uses an MLLM to summarize each page of a trajectory (description, key UI elements, action path, label) into a page chunk, vectorized and stored per-app in a Milvus database; coarse-to-fine planning schedules subtasks to apps then retrieves top-k=3 similar pages by cosine similarity to augment the LLM Planner; a dual-LLM (Decision-maker + Judge) executor tracks task progress via short-term memory across steps.
evaluacion: Evaluated on real Android devices (Xiaomi 14, ADB) with GPT-4o on SPA-Bench (340 tasks, single/cross-app, EN/ZH) and the CHOP dataset (60 tasks, 3 difficulty levels), compared against AutoDroid, AppAgent, MobileAgentV2, SeeAct and M3A, plus per-step time/token-cost measurement.
numeros_clave: SPA-Bench single-app success 0.627 EN/0.553 ZH vs M3A 0.640/0.447; cross-app 0.350/0.350 vs M3A 0.200/0.100; CHOP overall 0.800 EN/0.700 ZH vs best baseline 0.700/0.633; cost $0.040/step at 14.6s vs M3A $0.092/step at 19.3s.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the dual-LLM Judge maintains an explicit natural-language task-progress state (evaluation/progress/next-action, Eq.8-9) fed back into the Decision-maker each step, a concrete plan-state channel MF could adapt for tracking sub-goal completion.

coarse-to-fine retrieval (top-k=3 cosine similarity over page vectors, Eq.5) is measured end-to-end against 5 real baselines and drives the success-rate gains, supporting MF's bet on a measured retrieval layer over ad-hoc context stuffing.

Fig.3 explicitly plots mean token-cost-per-step (USD) and mean time-per-step, showing MapAgent reaches a better accuracy/cost trade-off than heavier baselines, external evidence for treating cost as a first-class metric.

notes: Numbers from Table 1/2 (SPA-Bench/CHOP results) and Fig.3 (cost-vs-time scatter); ablation Table 3 (memory+Judge) referenced in text.

cita: Fang et al. (2025). Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory.
problema: LLM agents suffer from brittle procedural memory that is either manually hand-engineered as prompt templates or entangled in static model parameters, so there is no systematic, learnable way to build, retrieve and update reusable procedural knowledge across trajectories.
mecanismo: Build (WRITE) distills past trajectories into fine-grained step-by-step Trajectory memories and higher-level Script abstractions (or their combination, Proceduralization), stored as raw trajectory text (DOCS-ARCHIVOS) and retrieved via query- or keyword-based (AveFact) vector matching (VECTOR); Update applies dynamic add (ADMISION), validation-filtering, reflexion and dynamic-discarding (OLVIDO) strategies (ACTUALIZACION) that periodically consolidate the memory bank as new experience arrives.
evaluacion: Evaluated on TravelPlanner and ALFWorld with GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-sonnet and Qwen2.5-72B backbones; ablations on memory granularity (Table1), retrieval key strategy (Table2), online update strategy (vanilla/validation/reflexion, Fig.3), and cross-model transfer (GPT-4o memory reused by Qwen2.5-14B).
numeros_clave: Proceduralization raises ALFWorld test success from 42.14% (no memory) to 87.14%/77.86% with GPT-4o; reflexion-based update beats the 2nd-best update strategy by +0.7 points and cuts 14 steps by the final trajectory group; transferring GPT-4o's memory to Qwen2.5-14B raises task completion by ~5% and cuts avg steps by 1.6.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the dynamic Update module (validation-filtering + reflexion + discarding, §4.3) directly measures which consolidation strategy best promotes successful trajectories into durable memory, supporting MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion design.

reports step-count reduction as a measured efficiency proxy for token/latency savings (Fig.1, Table1) — a cheap pattern MF could reuse to track context economy without instrumenting raw token counters.

the Validation/Adjustment update strategies (§4.3) explicitly guard against stale or erroneous memory entries by filtering to only successful trajectories, evidence for MF's anti-drift/staleness discipline.

notes: Numbers from Table 1 (Build ablation), Fig.3 (update-strategy reward/steps curves), Fig.5b (cross-model transfer), §4.2-4.4.

cita: Han et al. (2025). LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation.
problema: Multi-agent LLM workflow-automation systems (an orchestrator delegating to specialized task agents) remain stateless and transactional — each task is solved from scratch discarding prior experience — and no prior procedural-memory work addresses the placement/allocation problem specific to multi-agent coordination.
mecanismo: An offline construction phase (WRITE) distills successful trajectories into full-task memories (task description + high-level plan) and subtask memories (agent-specific tool traces), indexed by dense-embedding vector stores (VECTOR) per orchestrator and per task-agent; at inference three retrieval/allocation variants (vanilla, Dynamic just-in-time, QueryRewrite) allocate full-task memory to the orchestrator and subtask memory to each task agent (role-aware, MULTIAGENTE placement).
evaluacion: Evaluated on OfficeBench (300 multi-app office tasks, 148 train/152 test, 3 difficulty levels) across LLM-only (GPT-4o), Hybrid (GPT-4o orchestrator + GPT-4o-mini agents), and SLM-only (GPT-4o-mini) teams, against No-memory/Synapse/AWM baselines, with ablations on memory placement (orchestrator vs agent vs both) and retrieval variant.
numeros_clave: LEGOMem improves overall task success rate by +12.61%, +12.72%, +13.38% absolute over memory-less LLM/Hybrid/SLM teams respectively; Hybrid team + LEGOMem-QueryRewrite reaches 50.22% success, surpassing the memory-less full-LLM team's 45.83%; in the task-agent-only memory setting, Dynamic/QueryRewrite beat vanilla by 4-5% for Hybrid teams.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the orchestrator dynamically regenerates the next subtask from current state and can re-plan on stalled progress (§3.1.1, Algorithm 1) — an explicit plan/re-plan state machine MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could reuse.

Table2's placement ablation shows orchestrator memory and per-agent subtask memory are distinct, single-purpose stores whose separate placement (not one shared blob) drives most of the gain, evidence for single-source-per-fact allocation across roles.
three retrieval strategies (vanilla/Dynamic/QueryRewrite) are measured head-to-head on OfficeBench (Table2) rather than assumed, supporting MF's insistence on a measured retrieval layer.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main results) and Table2 (placement/retrieval ablation), §4.2 Main results.

cita: Cao et al. (2025). Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution.
problema: Existing procedural-memory frameworks follow a 'passive accumulation' paradigm — memory is a static append-only archive that is never adapted to new contexts nor pruned of harmful entries, so the experience pool degrades into a mixture of valid insights and toxic noise over time.
mecanismo: Multi-faceted distillation (WRITE/ADMISION) extracts success-pattern, failure-analysis and comparative-insight experiences from sampled trajectories, validated by an LLM judge and deduplicated before being embedded (VECTOR) by usage-scenario; context-adaptive reuse retrieves top-K by cosine similarity then reranks and rewrites experiences for the new task (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); utility-based refinement (CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION) tracks per-experience retrieval-frequency and utility, selectively adding only successful trajectories and pruning entries whose utility/frequency ratio falls below a threshold.
evaluacion: Evaluated on BFCL-V3 (150 test tasks) and AppWorld (168 test-normal tasks) with Qwen3-8B/14B/32B backbones, reporting Avg@4 and Pass@4 against No-Memory, A-Mem and LangMem baselines, plus ablations on extraction granularity (trajectory- vs keypoint-level, Table2) and on addition/reflection/deletion components (Table3).
numeros_clave: Qwen3-8B+ReMe(dynamic) beats No-Memory by 8.83% Avg@4 / 7.29% Pass@4 on average across benchmarks; on AppWorld Qwen3-8B rises from 14.97% (no memory) to 24.70% Avg@4 / 42.06% Pass@4; keypoint-level extraction (44.50/65.77) beats trajectory-level (43.00/60.00) on BFCL-V3 for Qwen3-8B (Table2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: utility-based deletion (Eq.1, §3.4) explicitly measures which memories to keep vs prune based on a retrieval-utility ratio, directly supporting promotion/demotion of gotchas into durable recipes.

ablation Table3 shows selective addition (only successful trajectories) outperforms full addition (which also distills failures) because failure-derived entries introduce noise, evidence memory must guard provenance/quality rather than just accumulate.

the abstract's memory-scaling claim (small Qwen3-8B+ReMe beats larger memory-less Qwen3-14B) is framed as a compute-efficiency argument relevant to MF's context-economy lens, though token/latency cost itself is not directly measured.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main BFCL-V3/AppWorld results), Table2 (granularity ablation), Table3 (component ablation).

cita: Wang et al. (2026). EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization.
problema: LLM-based code-efficiency optimization methods operate instance-by-instance (one-shot rewriting, retrieved exemplars, or search-based rewriting) and never distill reusable optimization knowledge, so recurring slow-to-fast transformation mechanisms are re-discovered per task rather than captured once and reused across tasks.
mecanismo: Stage I (offline WRITE/CONSOLIDACION) mines large-scale slow/fast program pairs into structured traces, abstracts them into signatures, hybrid-clusters (TF-IDF + embeddings) and distills each cluster into a documented 'Operator Skill' or higher-level 'Meta Skill' card stored as a skill-card file library (DOCS-ARCHIVOS); Stage II applies the library execution-free at inference — diagnosis, skill retrieval (3 candidate sets, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO), plan composition (2-3 plans per bundle) and candidate generation, without any runtime execution feedback.
evaluacion: Evaluated on EffiBench-X (623 tasks, Python and C++ subsets, execution-based runtime measurement) with GPT-5-mini and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct backbones, against prompting/retrieval/search-based baselines including SBLLM, using a public/private test split for candidate ranking and final correctness/efficiency scoring.
numeros_clave: Improves optimization success rate over the strongest baseline by 3.69-12.52 percentage points across settings: +12.03pp (C++) and +4.98pp (Python) with GPT-5-mini; +12.36pp (C++) and +8.67pp (Python) with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Operator/Meta Skill cards (Fig.2) are explicit typed narrative documents (skill_id, triggers, transformation steps, pitfalls) mined offline and reused as ground truth at inference, a concrete pattern for MF's typed-docs-as-truth Tier-1.

Stage I explicitly clusters and merges near-duplicate mined traces (TF-IDF cosine merge threshold 0.8, §3.2) into a compact skill library, direct evidence for promoting scattered instance-level lessons into durable, deduplicated recipes.

the execution-free inference design (no runtime candidate-execution feedback loop, §2.1) trades a larger offline mining cost for near-zero per-task inference compute, a pattern relevant to MF's context-economy tradeoffs.

notes: Numbers from Abstract and §4 (EffiBench-X results per language/backbone); skill-card structure in Fig.2, §3.2 mining pipeline.

cita: Cheng et al. (2026). Mem2Evolve: Towards Self-Evolving Agents via Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation.
problema: Existing self-evolving agent frameworks treat experience-accumulation and capability-creation (new tools/expert agents) as isolated processes: experience-centric methods stay bounded by a fixed pre-defined toolset, while capability-centric methods create new assets from scratch with no experiential guidance, causing unstable, non-replicable capability growth.
mecanismo: A dual-memory design couples Asset Memory (agent bank + tool bank, structured records combining role/expertise text and executable tool code — HIBRIDA) with Experience Memory (title/context/use-cases/distilled-knowledge records, WRITE); forward inference recruits from Asset Memory by similarity or creates new tools/agents on-demand guided by retrieved experience (ADMISION + RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, MULTIAGENTE recruitment of expert agents); backward evolution runs an LLM-judge trajectory evaluation, a self-correction/test-validation loop before persisting new assets (FIDELIDAD), then reflects to distill success/failure lessons and merges them into Experience Memory (ACTUALIZACION/CONSOLIDACION).
evaluacion: Evaluated across 6 task categories and 8 benchmarks (GAIA, ALFWorld, WebShop, TravelPlanner, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, AIME24/25) with GPT-5-chat, against naive-LLM, experience-centric (DyLAN, EvoAgent, AFLOW, DSPy) and capability-centric (Alita, AgentVerse, AutoAgents, SwarmAgentic) baselines, plus an ablation removing Tool Creation / Expert-Agent Creation / Experience Distillation (Table3).
numeros_clave: Mem2Evolve reaches 70.24% avg Pass@1 across 8 benchmarks, beating naive-LLM by 18.53%, experience-centric best (AFLOW) by 11.80%, capability-centric best (Alita) by 6.46%; on GAIA it gains +57.84% Pass@1 over a minimal-toolset baseline; ablation shows removing Tool Creation causes the largest drop (-10.28%), removing Expert-Agent Creation -1.72%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: backward evolution explicitly promotes only validated, test-passing assets and reflected lessons into persistent memory (§3.3.2-3.3.3), a direct instance of consolidating transient trial outcomes into durable recipes.
new tools/agents must pass an LLM-synthesized test suite (Valid(mnew,ct), Eq.8) before being merged into Asset Memory, guarding against poisoning the capability store with unreliable assets.

splitting memory into a typed Asset Memory (tools/agents) versus Experience Memory (lessons) with distinct schemas (Eq.1-4) is a concrete multi-store seam design MF's COSTURAS anchor could compare against.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (main 8-benchmark Pass@1) and Table3/§5.1 (ablation: -10.28%/-1.72%).
